sheet-8.description: This single sheet, printed as sheet 8 of the New Milford atlas and dated August 1930, covers the River Edge Manor Section on the west side of New Milford, Bergen County, at 100 feet to an inch. The Hackensack River runs down the upper left corner, with a large unsubdivided tract (block 103) along its east bank. River Road crosses the sheet from the northeast corner to the bottom, curving southwest from Cedar Road and then running south past Monmouth Avenue to Henley Avenue. North of River Road the sheet shows Voorhis Avenue (formerly Demarest Avenue) along the top, Albert Place, Hughes Place, Cedar Road (Linwood Avenue) and Holland Avenue, laid out in narrow residential lots. To the west, River Edge Avenue runs diagonally from the river toward River Road, with Columbia (Riverside Avenue) and Harvard (Riverview Avenue) leaving it to the south. The southern half is a regular grid of 50 ft streets: Zabriskie Place, Monmouth Avenue and Henley Avenue running east and west, and Trenton, Stockton, Berkley and Asbury running north and south, with Columbia, Harvard and Yale south of Henley Avenue. Audrey Place and the southern ends of Columbia and Harvard are marked not open. Building is sparse: scattered one and two storey frame dwellings with auto garages, a filling station near River Road and Voorhis Avenue, and Fire Department No. 2 on Trenton Street south of Monmouth Avenue. Six inch water pipes are drawn in most streets. Asbury is drawn with only its west side, at the east edge of the sheet; the bottom row of blocks is marked no exposure.
notes: Printed sheet number 8; the River Edge Manor Section of New Milford.

Modern names: Hughes Place is Hughes Road; Cedar Road (Linwood Avenue) east of River Road is Cedar Road; Columbia, Harvard, Yale, Trenton, Stockton, Berkley and Asbury are now Streets (Columbia Street, Harvard Street, Yale Street, Trenton Street, Stockton Street, Berkley Street, Asbury Street).
Berkley Street and Asbury Street now continue north to Cedar Road through ground shown undivided on the sheet (block 115).
The modern Hughes Road / Cedar Road junction lies about 8 m from the drawn one; the Monmouth Avenue / River Road junction disagrees with the fit by about 8 m (River Road realigned there).
